newsitem.title: USA: Widespread showers headed for western Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Widespread showers headed for western Midwest.

text.p: Rain should cover much of the western Midwest now through Friday bringing moisture to even the dry areas of western Iowa, meteorologists said.

"We are looking for numerous showers and thunderstorms covering most of Iowa, eastern Nebraska, northern Missouri, northern Illinois and southern Wisconsin the next 48 hours," said Joel Burgio, agricultural meteorologist at Weather Services Corp.
Burgio estimated rain amounts at 0.50 to two inches and "coverage will be quite high."
"It would be favorable for the crops," he said.
Rains should reach the eastern Midwest Saturday and continue through Sunday, he said.
Weather Express Inc meteorologist Fred Gesser said the rains this week and early next week should restore soil moisture in much of the Midwest dry areas.
"After this system today and the one Sunday and Monday, the remaining dry area will be on a line (in Illinois) from Moline to Peoria to Springfield," Gesser said.
Temperatures may peak in the low 90s degrees Fahrenheit Monday and Tuesday in the Midwest and slip back to range from 70s to low 80s the rest of the week, meteorologists said.
